newsitem.title: CANADA: Chemical prices, writedown pressure NOVA profits.
newsitem.headline: Chemical prices, writedown pressure NOVA profits.

text.p: Canadian pipeline and petrochemical firm NOVA Corp on Tuesday reported lower earnings in 1996 compared to the year-earlier period because of lower chemical prices and a writedown in its Methanex Corp investment.
Despite the lower profits, NOVA said its low-cost petrochemical operations and higher pipeline returns kept results at strong levels.
Net income from continuing operations for year was C$463 million or C$0.98 per share, down from C$702 million or C$1.44 per share in 1995.

However, total earnings for the year were cut by C$32 million or C$0.07 per share to C$431 million or C$0.91 per share after 25-percent owned Methanex wrote down the value of methanol production assets to be idled, NOVA said.
The company said its NOVA Chemicals unit contributed C$217 million to corporate earnings in 1996, down C$291 million from the 1995 record earnings of C$508 million.T
The drop was a result of lower selling prices and higher crude oil feedstock costs in 1996, it said, adding that increased sales volumes helped to offset the effect of lower margins.
NOVA said polyethylene benchmark prices, which started the year at US$0.32 per pound, rose to a high of US$0.47 in the third quarter.
"The year end benchmark price of US$0.44 per pound is expected to rise in early 1997 as producers respond to much higher feedstock costs," NOVA said.

Through 1996, polystyrene benchmark prices experienced an 18 percent decline mostly because of increased industry capacity, NOVA said. A price increase has also been announced for polystyrene by February 15.

NOVA said its NOVA Gas Transmission Ltd subsidiary contributed C$181 million to profits in 1996, up C$15 million from the year before, because of higher earnings from the system's incentive settlement with shippers and expansion of the pipeline. Investment base growth increased NGT's earnings by C$5 million when compared to the prior year's results, it said.
Capital spending for 1996 was C$255 million, compared to C$584 million in 1995 and the company said it expected to spend about C$500 million in 1997 on the pipeline system.

NOVA said NOVA Gas International's income contribution was C$66 million, up from C$31 million in 1995. Much of the increase came as a result of stronger performance from affiliated energy services giant NGC Corp, it said.
